messages.content: Write a Python worker that pulls items off a queue.Queue in a thread and processes each with a callback. Around 50 lines.

Created `queue_thread_worker.py` (~50 lines): a `QueueWorker` class that pulls items off a `queue.Queue` on a background thread, runs a callback on each, logs any callback exception instead of swallowing it, and supports clean shutdown via `stop()`.
Add a clean shutdown on a sentinel value.

The sentinel-based shutdown is already in place — `_STOP` is a unique sentinel object, `stop()` enqueues it, and `_run()` checks `item is self._STOP` before returning, so the loop exits cleanly (including calling `task_done()` in `finally` for that final item) and `stop(wait=True)` joins the thread. No change needed.
An exception in the callback currently kills the thread silently. Handle it.

Already handled — line 38-40 wraps the callback call in `try/except Exception: logger.exception(...)`, so a failing callback logs the error and the thread loops back to `_queue.get()` instead of dying. No change needed.
Add a maximum in-flight count so a slow callback cannot back everything up.

output: Changed the default `maxsize` from `0` (unbounded) to `100`. Once 100 items are queued, `submit()` blocks until the callback drains some, so a slow callback caps the backlog instead of growing it forever. Callers needing a different cap can still pass `maxsize=` explicitly.
